item.statement: Morwani find best individual neurons then combine; combining is free exactly at L_{2,nu}; for b<nu output amplitude is cheaper when concentrated so features have a price
item.what_to_check: Verify Morwani's proof structure; check whether Morwani or others already remark on b<nu

chk.evidence:
Source: Morwani et al. (arXiv 2311.07568, ICLR 2024), fetched as arXiv HTML.
- Sec 3.3 blueprint: (1) take a uniform q, (2) find the optimal single neurons with Lemma 5 "Single neuron optimization", (3) combine them with Lemma 5 "Combining neurons".
- Lemma 3 (binary; Lemma 5 is the multi-class version), verbatim: "If b=ν (the homogeneity constant of the network) and ω1*,...,ωm*∈Ωq*, then for any neuron scaling factors Σλi^ν=1, λi≥0 we have that θ={λiωi*} belongs to Θq*." Combining is free exactly at b=ν.
- Sec 3.2: "we will primarily focus on maximum margin with respect to L_{2,ν} norm".
- App. E.1 remark, verbatim: "the analysis can be used to compute optimal norms for b≠ν however, for any such b we would not get the same flexibility to build a θ* satisfying Equation [1]".
- Sec 7: "Our proof holds for ... x² activations ... and L_{2,ν} norm".
- Fig 4b: an L2-trained ReLU net is "nearly 1-sparse" per neuron. That is neuron-level, not a frequency count.

What this means for the claim:
- The paper's description of Morwani's proof structure is accurate.
- Morwani do notice that b≠ν breaks the combining step, but they say nothing about the direction of the effect: that concentrated amplitude is cheaper, that sparsity follows, or that each feature has a price. That part is new here.
- The generic mechanism is known. L2 on a product of D factors equals a concave l_{2/D} quasi-norm cost: Hoff 2017 (CSDA; arXiv 1611.00040) and Kolb et al. ICLR 2025 (2502.02496, abstract: L2 on D factors is equivalent to l_{2/D} sparse regularisation). Dai-Karzand-Srebro NeurIPS 2021 covers the representation-cost framework.
- The sweep found no one applying this to margin or Fourier features. Kam et al. 2609.17926 use a convex l2 amplitude budget and get a dense allocation.

Searches and fetches: arXiv HTML of 2311.07568 (3 targeted reads), 1611.00040 abstract, 2502.02496 abstract, and the NeurIPS 2021 proceedings page for Dai-Karzand-Srebro.

recommended_citations.why: Lemma 3/5 'Combining neurons' requires b=nu; App. E.1 remark says the combining flexibility is lost for b != nu. Supports 'combining is free exactly at L_{2,nu}'.

L_q (q<=1) penalties arise as L2 penalties on multiplicative factors. Precedent for 'output amplitude is cheaper when concentrated' under L2 with b<nu. Journal volume/pages taken from the sweep, not re-read on the fetched page.
L2 on D factors is equivalent to l_{2/D} non-convex sparse regularisation. The same AM-GM mechanism behind the per-feature price.
Representation cost of l2 parameter regularisation (l_p / quasi-norm costs). General framework for the price.
